Green Synthesis of Magnetic Supramolecules β‑Cyclodextrin/Iron
Oxide Nanoparticles for Photocatalytic and Antibacterial
Applications
Tahani M. Almutairi, Hessa H. Al-Rasheed, Zainab M. Alaqil, Amira K. Hajri, and Nadia H. Elsayed*
Cite This: ACS Omega 2023, 8, 32067−32077

ACCESS

ABSTRACT: Iron oxide nanoparticles (Fe3O4NPs) are a fascinating field of
study due to their wide range of practical applications in environmental and
medical contexts. This study presents a straightforward, environmentally
friendly method for producing Fe3O4NPs utilizing β-cyclodextrin (β-CD) as a
reducing and capping agent. This approach results in the rapid and effective
eco-friendly synthesis of β-CD/Fe3O4NPs. The properties and characteristics
of β-CD/Fe3O4NPs were investigated using various methods, including
ultraviolet−visible (UV/vis) spectroscopy, Fourier transform infrared (FTIR)
spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), transmission electron
microscopy (TEM), X-ray diffraction (XRD), thermogravimetry analysis
(TGA), and vibrating-sample magnetometry (VSM). The absorption of β-
CD/Fe3O4NPs caused a distinct peak at 349 nm, as evidenced by the results
of UV/vis studies. This peak was attributed to the absorption of surface
plasmon resonance. The crystalline nature of β-CD/Fe3O4NPs was confirmed through XRD analysis. The SEM and TEM analyses
have verified the geometry and structural characteristics of β-CD/Fe3O4NPs. The β-CD/Fe3O4NPs exhibited remarkable
effectiveness in the decomposing efficiency (%) of methylene blue (MB) dye with 52.2, 94.1, and 100% for 0.2, 0.4, and 0.6 g β-CD/
Fe3O4NPs, respectively. In addition, the highest efficiency in hunting radicals was observed (347.2 ± 8.2 mg/g) at 100 mg/mL β-
CD/Fe3O4NPs; the combination of β-CD/Fe3O4NPs exhibited remarkable effectiveness in inhibiting the growth of some bacteria
that cause infections. The capabilities of β-CD/Fe3O4NPs for various applications showed that these materials could be used in
photocatalytic, antioxidants, and antibacterial. Additionally, the eco-friendly synthesis of these materials makes them a promising
option for the remediation of harmful pollutants and microbes.
1. INTRODUCTION
In recent times, green synthesis has garnered considerable
attention as a means of producing nanoparticles (NPs); this is
the increasing demand for eco-conscious techniques for creating
NPs.1 Numerous designs are accessible for producing NPs,
including chemical, hydrothermal, solvothermal, and physical
approaches.2 The intricate techniques of physical processes are
ineffective in managing the NP size. One of the primary
drawbacks is the inconsistency in particle size, coupled with the
relatively high manufacturing expenses.3 Conversely, using
chemical techniques necessitates using harmful solvents, making
them detrimental to the environment. Likewise, the methods of
hydrothermal and solvothermal nature require a significant
amount of energy.4 As a result, the production of nanoparticles
through green synthesis has received widespread approval due to
its utilization of harmless biomolecules, which increases the
possibility of dispensing dangerous substances that would have
been present in the chemical synthesis.5 Polysaccharides are one
of these biomolecules that utilize as reducing and capping agents
for metal nanoparticle synthesis and significantly decrease the
overall expenses of the procedure.6 Different metal NPs, such as
silver, gold, selenium, and nickel, have been produced using
natural sources.7 NPs are stabilized by various −OH and
−COOH groups in polysaccharides, which serve as reducing,
capping, and stabilizing agents.8 These NPs have the potential to
function as antioxidants and exhibit anticancer properties.9
Cyclodextrin is a type of polysaccharide that has gained
significant interest in environmental remediation.10 This green
and harmless polysaccharide is produced through enzymatic
activity on a lengthy amylose.11 β-CD is a cyclic oligosaccharide
with seven α-D-glucose units linked together through α-(1,4)
connections. These molecules have a unique shape that
resembles cones.12 They have a central opening that is polar

and surrounded by primary hydroxyl groups on the outer
surface.13 The inner surface contains secondary hydroxyl
groups. The hydrophobic cavity of cyclodextrins can create
inclusion complexes with a diverse range of organic and
inorganic compounds.14
Iron oxide nanomagnets have caught the attention of
researchers due to their distinctive internal characteristics,
capability to bond with bioactive substances, and ability to
remain stable in the colloidal form.15 The biosynthesis of
magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs) through β-CD has numerous
advantages. These include remarkable biocompatibility, afford-
ability, impressive magnetic properties, easy surface modifica-
tion, excellent recovery, high porosity, density, and stability.16
Additionally, the wide surface area of β-CD provides many
adsorption sites, resulting in various beneficial impacts. The
original shape of iron oxide nanomagnets has attracted the
attention of numerous researchers because of their chemical and
biological characteristics.17 The potential applications of MNPs
are diverse and include fields such as biomedicine, bioremedia-
tion, electronics, agriculture, and energy.18
The world faces numerous problems due to rising environ-
mental pollution.19 The movement of pollutants from their
origin through air, water, and soil exacerbates harmful
conditions.20 The leading causes of environmental contami-
nation are microbial pathogens and dyes.21 It is imperative to
explore the environmentally conscious properties of nanoma-
terials, such as their ability to combat harmful microorganisms
and eliminate dyes from the surroundings.22 The adsorption
potential of β-CD is significant due to the interaction between
host and guest molecules in supramolecular chemistry and the
synergistic effect.13,23
Furthermore, by incorporating the magnetic characteristics of
iron oxide, β-CD can create adsorbents that can be effortlessly
extracted from a water-based solution by applying an external
magnetic force.24 The cooperative agents generate a complex of
β-CD with iron oxide nanomagnet components that act as the
magnetic carrier. This combination guarantees the spread of
materials and benefits effortless recycling. So, in this study, β-
CD/Fe3O4NPs were fabricated for use in some applications.
Methylene blue (MB) dye is widely discussed and demands
cautious treatment before it is introduced into the aquatic
environment.25 There are multiple ways to treat water, such as
utilizing adsorption, chemical oxidation, photocatalytic degra-
dation, electrochemical degradation, and heterogeneous catal-
ysis.26 Unlike the conventional adsorption technique that
effectively eliminates dye from wastewater but requires a tedious
process of regenerating the adsorbent, most of the methods
discussed are costly, inefficient, and nondestructive to organic
pollutants, leading to time-consuming processes.27 It has been
determined through extensive research that photodegradation
can effectively break down hazardous organic contaminants into
harmless compounds 27 when subjected to a specific type of
light.
It was reported that Fe3O4NPs were utilized to create a
magnetic substance by incorporating immobilized carboxy-
methyl, β-CD, and cyanamide as the linking agent. This
substance was then employed to adsorb Cu2+ and methyl
green.28 In another approach, it is possible to create flower-
shaped Fe3O4 particles modified with a porous β-CD polymer
(β-CDP@Fe3O4). This modification is intended to eliminate a
range of organic contaminants from water. The successful
elimination of organic pollutants was credited to the diverse
noncovalent connections between β-CDP@Fe3O4 and the
impurities. These connections include hydrophobic interac-
tions, hydrogen bonds, π−π, and electrostatic interactions. The
findings indicate that CDP@Fe3O4 has the potential to be used
for purifying complex organic wastewater due to its exceptional
photocatalytic features and easy regeneration process.29
In this study, the eco-friendly synthesis of Fe3O4NPs using β-
CD as a stabilizing and reducing agent produces β-CD/
Fe3O4NPs. The aim was to create an affordable and environ-
mentally friendly method for the effectiveness of β-CD/
Fe3O4NPs to determine their efficacy in photocatalytic,
antioxidant, and antimicrobial applications.
2. MATERIALS AND METHODS
2.1. Material and Bacterial Strains. The purest form of all
of the chemicals was utilized without any further purification,

and they were all of analytical grade. The FeCl3·6H2O
compound was procured from Sigma-Aldrich, based in the
United States. Beijing Chemical Works provided the experi-
ment’s MB, NaOH, and 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl (DPPH).
Gram-negative Escherichia coli strains JCL16 and Gram-positive
Bacillus subtilis were procured from the CGMCC in Beijing,
China. These bacterial strains are known to cause diseases. Milli-
Q H2O was utilized to prepare all of the aqueous solutions.
2.2. Green Synthesis of Magnetic β-CD/Fe3O4NPs. The
synthesis of supramolecular nanoparticles with magnetic
properties involved β-CD/Fe3O4NPs using β-CD. The process
followed a previously published method with some modifica-
tions,30 which utilized the co-precipitation of Fe3O4NPs in a
water-based solution. The reaction was carried out at 70 °C
under a nitrogen atmosphere in the presence of NH4OH. On the
other hand, the novelty in this research was based on the
amalgamation carried out through a one-pot process, where the
Fe3O4NPs were created and secured by β-CD as a colloidal
aqueous solution. The process did not necessitate the dispersion
of the nanoparticles in a polymer medium.
To summarize, a solution of β-CD (2.0% w/v, 100 mL) was
vigorously stirred and heated to 40 °C, following which FeCl3
(0.04 M) was added to it dropwise. Afterward, the temperature
was raised to 70 °C while exposed to a nitrogen environment.
The reaction flask was then blended with 12 mL of NH4OH
solution (20.0% v/v) and stirred moderately for 20 min. Then,
the solution was brought to ambient temperature and subjected
to dialysis for a day utilizing a cellulose filter (with a molecular
weight cutoff of 12 kDa) while gently agitating at room
temperature. After the refinement process, the colloidal mixture
was preserved at 8 ± 2 °C for future use.
2.3. Characterization of β-CD/Fe3O4NPs. UV−visible
spectroscopy (Shimadzu-2450) confirmed the formation of β-
CD/Fe3O4NPs that were synthesized biologically. The wave-
length ranging from 200 to 800 nm was examined. An analysis
was conducted on the structural properties of β-CD/Fe3O4NPs
using an X-ray diffractometer (XRD Rigaku Miniflex). The
device was powered by a 30 mA and 40 KV current and utilized a
Cu Kα radiation (1.5405 Å). Also, the β-CD/Fe3O4NPs were
examined using a Hitachi s-4200 N scanning electron micro-
scope (SEM), and a transmission electron microscope (TEM,
Phillip CM12) was utilized to analyze their structural character-
istics and morphology. TGA (PerkinElmer TGA7) was used to
determine the thermal stability of β-CD/Fe3O4NPs. The
experiment was conducted under a nitrogen atmosphere with
a heating rate of 25 °C/min. The Lake Shore model 7404 VSM
from the USA was utilized to measure magnetization curves
concerning temperature.

2.4. Photocatalytic Depletion of MB over β-CD/
Fe3O4NPs. The effectiveness of β-CD/Fe3O4NPs was evaluated
through a photocatalytic experiment where the degradation of
MB dye was observed under visible light exposure from a 100 W
tungsten lamp. The potential of β-CD/Fe3O4NPs to break down
substances was demonstrated by monitoring MB while
constantly agitating and exposing it to visible light. A stock
MB solution was created by blending 10 mg/L MB in 50 mL of
Milli-Q H2O to form an aqueous solution. After mixing 25 mL of
MB solution with 0.2, 0.4, and 0.6 g β-CD/Fe3O4NPs, the
solution was subjected to magnetic stirring for half an hour
without light to establish the state of adsorption and desorption
equilibrium. The blend of substances was subsequently exposed
to the tungsten lamp with constant agitation. Throughout the

entire trial, the temperature was maintained at 30 °C. Samples of
the mixture were collected at regular intervals and subjected to
centrifugation at a speed of 2000 rpm for 5 min. Next, the
gathered supernatant underwent analysis using UV−vis spec-
troscopy (Shimadzu-2450) at a wavelength of 664 nm to
investigate the degradation of MB through photocatalysis. The
procedure persisted until the complete disintegration of the dye.
Moreover, a trial run was conducted without the presence of β-
CD/Fe3O4NPs to observe any color changes.
2.5. Antioxidant Activity of β-CD/Fe3O4NPs. The β-CD/
Fe3O4NPs were tested for their antioxidant properties by using
them against stable DPPH, as previously published.31 The
benchmark for comparison was set by Vitamin C. Various
amounts of β-CD/Fe3O4NPs (0.25−2.0 mg/mL) were
combined with 0.5 mL of DPPH (1 mM) dissolved in methanol.
The mixture was then incubated in the dark at room
temperature. Following the incubation process, the UV
absorbance of the specimens was determined using a UV
spectrophotometer (UVmini-1240; Shimadzu, Japan) at 517
nm with methanol as the reference. The DPPH solution and
methanol without β-CD/Fe3O4NPs were used for the negative
control. The experiment was conducted in three sets, and the
scavenging activity percentage of β-CD/Fe3O4NPs was

2.6. Antibacterial Activity of β-CD/Fe3O4NPs. The zone
of inhibition (ZOI) diameter was utilized against Gram-positive
(B. subtilis) and Gram-negative (E. coli) to evaluate the
antibacterial effectiveness of the β-CD/Fe3O4NPs. The data
obtained were compared to that gathered from typical antibiotic
disks (30 μg of Gentamicin). After sterilizing the nutrient agar
through boiling, it was carefully moved onto the Petri dishes
using aseptic techniques and incubated for 20 min. A Petri dish’s
surface was inoculated using a sterile loop with a single colony
from each bacterial strain. After that, β-CD/Fe3O4NPs and a
standard antibiotic were placed on a Petri dish with nutrient
agar. The dish was then incubated at 37 °C for 24 h. By
conducting three experimental replicates, the diameter of ZOI
was established.32
2.7. Statistical Evaluation. Three repetitions of the tests
were executed, and the statistical evaluation was carried out with
the aid of Medcalc software version 15.0 (Medcalc 15.0,
Mariakerke, and Belgium). The continuous variables were
analyzed by calculating the mean and standard deviation,
statistical measures of central tendency, and variability.
3. RESULTS AND DISCUSSION
3.1. Optical Characteristics. The study of optical proper-
ties has been traditionally carried out through UV/vis
absorption spectroscopy.33 Figure 1 displays a broad absorption
spectrum at 349 nm in the UV−visible spectra of the β-CD/
Fe3O4NPs that were synthesized. The magnetic nanoparticles
can absorb UV light within the range of 330−450 nm due to how
the light is absorbed and scattered by the particles.34 Prior
studies have yielded comparable outcomes.35 In addition, it is
possible to attribute the alteration in the hue of the initial
solution from a yellow shade to a darker one as the synthesis
process progresses to the surface plasmon resonance excitation
phenomenon.36
3.2. FTIR Spectroscopy. The current investigation
conducted Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy
analysis to categorize the functional groups present in
biomolecule β-CD, employed to reduce and cap FeCl3, resulting
in the formation of β-CD/Fe3O4NPs (as illustrated in Figure 2).
The existence of the −OH stretching group in β-CD was verified
by the spectral bands observed at wave numbers of 3470 cm−1.
Upon interaction with an iron salt, the band shifts to 3399 cm−1,
exhibiting increased broadening. The spectral feature observed
at a wavenumber of 2945 cm−1 can be attributed to the
stretching vibration of the C−H functional group. The presence
of spectral bands at approx. 1601 cm−1 may be ascribed to the

Furthermore, an analysis was conducted on the zone ranging

The Fe−O bands that are distinctive can be recognized in the
magnetite phases. The Fe3O4 compound exhibited a wide
spectral band at 540 cm−1 and a secondary peak at approximately
719 cm−1. This phenomenon was ascribed to the process of
surface oxidation.39
3.3. XRD Analysis. The crystallinity and size of the
synthesized β-CD/Fe3O4NPs have been investigated through
XRD analysis. The XRD outcomes indicated that the β-CD/
Fe3O4NPs that were produced possessed a high degree of
crystallinity. The study detected multiple peaks at various 2θ
values of 32.1, 36.8, 44.3, 55.1, 62.7, and 73.5° (Figure 3),
ranging from 10 to 80°, which were identified as corresponding
to specific lattice planes, including 220, 311, 400, 422, 511, and
440. These findings were consistent with the literature-reported
peaks and matched well with the cubic spinel structure of the
Fe3O4 crystalline phase.29 A graphical representation of the
observed peaks is provided in Figure 3. No more diffraction
peaks for β-CD/Fe3O4NPs were detected, indicating a notable
level of crystallinity. The estimated crystal size of β-CD/
Fe3O4NPs is identified using the Scherrer formula, which
involves analyzing the XRD line broadening.40

The formula for determining the average crystallite size (D)
involves several variables, including the wavelength of the X-ray
beam constant (λ = 0.1540 nm), the Bragg’s diffraction angle
(θ), and the half-maximum of the full width of the peak (β). As

studies.30
3.4. TGA of β-CD/Fe3O4NPs. Figure 4 displays a TGA plot
that exhibits a steady decrease in weight from 0 to 800 °C. From
0 to 200 °C, the weight loss in the composite was due to
eliminating water and any other solvents. It was previously
documented that comparable findings regarding weight
reduction were caused by confined moisture on β-CD/
Fe3O4NPs. A significant decrease in mass starting after 250 °C
for pure β-CD was due to the dehydration of hydroxyl groups
and carbonization of organic species. The total weight loss of β-
CD/Fe3O4NPs was 47.4%, and the enhanced thermal stability
was attributed to incorporating spinal MNPs. The breakdown of
the biological components in the solution may be linked to the
encapsulation of the artificially produced iron oxide nano-
particles. The disintegration caused by heat can serve as
additional evidence of the existence of β-CD incorporated into
the nanoparticles. An earlier study documented comparable
outcomes of the thermal breakdown of biomolecules layered on
the nanoparticles.30
3.5. VSM of β-CD/Fe3O4NPs. The magnetizable properties
of the nanoparticle samples make them a suitable choice for the
core of a reusable photocatalyst, as a magnet can easily attract
them. The VSM analysis was conducted to obtain the hysteresis
loops and determine the values of magnetization saturation
(Ms), remanence (Mr), and coercive field (Hc). It was observed

that a well-saturated M H loop41 was created, indicating that the
Mr and Hc values were not zero, thus confirming the
ferromagnetic nature of the sample. Figure 5 illustrates the
magnetic properties of the β-CD/Fe3O4NPs, depicting a super
magnetic property equal to 68.4 emu/g. The bulk value of
saturation magnetization is higher in the case of smaller
magnetic particles due to the ordered layers in the surface spin
of the NPs.42
Additionally, the Mr measurement of 13.76 × 10−3 emu/g
strongly correlates with the Ms values. The size of the
nanoparticles influenced the coercive field (294.83 Qe). When

3.6. Morphology and Elemental Composition. Mor-
phological analysis of β-CD/Fe3O4NPs was conducted using
TEM and SEM methods. The SEM graphs demonstrate that the
NPs produced are predominantly spherical. Also, the findings
indicated that some of the β-CD/Fe3O4NPs had oblong or
rounded shapes (Figure 6a). It is common for biological
synthesis to produce nanoparticles of varying sizes and shapes.44
The clustering of β-CD/Fe3O4NPs was apparent. The nano-
particles’ tiny size indicates promising potential for catalytic,
improved antibacterial, and antioxidant performance, attributed
to their amplified surface area.45
TEM was utilized to verify the morphology of the β-CD/
Fe3O4NPs; Figure 6b displays TEM micrographs revealing the
minuscule magnetite particles that are uniform in size and shape
and arranged uniformly with a conglomerate formation. The β-
CD/Fe3O4NPs combination exhibits a perfectly round structure
and is evenly distributed. The size of the particles was
determined to be 21.2 ± 2.1 nm using ImageJ software. Multiple
hydroxyl and carboxyl groups are common in β-CD, crucial in
creating a nanomagnetic.46 The crystal planes can be defined by
absorbing functional groups, like stabilizers and surfactants, or
by using a covering material that chelates with Fe atoms to create
a steric block. The scanning electron diffraction (SAED)
patterns depicted in Figure 6c exhibit distinct circular spots
organized in a configuration resembling a ring. Figure 6d
represents the DLS which showed the particle size closer to
TEM (22.8 nm). These patterns were analyzed to identify the
primary lattice planes present in the β-CD/Fe3O4NPs that were
produced, revealing that the nanoparticles are polycrystalline.
3.7. Photocatalytic Properties. The utilization of MB is
prevalent in the textile and dye processing sectors, leading to

significant ecological issues in aquatic environments. Visible
light does not cause any degradation of the MB.47 Visible light
irradiation (100 W tungsten lamps) was used to investigate the
efficiency of β-CD/Fe3O4NPs in breaking down MB through
photocatalysis. The absence of a catalyst in the MB solution was
used as a control, resulting in an absorption peak of 664 nm.
Figure 7a−c illustrates that incorporating biogenic β-CD/
Fe3O4NPs resulted in accelerated degradation of MB within
short, consistent time intervals (60 min in total). The gradual
decrease in the periodic absorbance peak of MB at 664 nm, while
the decomposition efficiency (%) was 52.2, 94.1, and 100% for
0.2, 0.4, and 0.6 g β-CD/Fe3O4NPs, respectively, suggested that
the dye was being broken down in stages. Below 0.2 and above
0.6 g of photocatalyst, the dose is not sufficient, and aggregation
takes place at a high dose hindering the light, and consequently,
the degradation efficiency declined. 0.6 g β-CD/Fe3O4NPs took
only an hour to observe the total breakdown of the MB
compared to other materials, as based on Table 1. The latest
research discloses that the combination of β-CD and Fe3O4NPs
exhibits remarkable photocatalytic performance and can be
efficiently employed as a photocatalyst to purify MB by virtue of
their superior photocatalytic characteristics.28
3.8. Reusability Test. The outcomes of the reusability
examination of the samples β-CD/Fe3O4NPs with different
contents are depicted in Figure 7d. The MB degradation
percentages for 0.2 g β-CD/Fe3O4NPs, 0.4 g β-CD/Fe3O4NPs,
and 0.6 g β-CD/Fe3O4NPs were 45.2, 91.3, and 95.7%,
respectively, as demonstrated. These degradation percentages
remain relatively constant with a very loss amount from their
original degradation % even after over five cycles. It is evident
from the results of both experiments that the use of β-CD/
Fe3O4NPs positively impacts the photostability. In addition,
using green synthesis improves the degradation efficiency.48
However, it does not have any impact on the ability of the
catalyst to be reused.
3.9. Mechanism. The behavior observed can be described as
a result of the interaction between Fe3O4 nanoparticles and MB
molecules. This interaction involves oxidation and reduction
processes, with the surface of the nanoparticles serving as a
platform for the absorption of the MB molecules. As a result, the
Fe3O4 NPs provide active locations for the electron interactions
between the organic dyes and nanoparticles. The photocatalytic
mechanism is the way to go when breaking down organic dyes.
This process involves exciting the dye using visible light with a
wavelength greater than 400 nm, which moves it from its ground
state (Dye0) to a triplet excited state (Dye*). In the course of
this process, the stimulated condition pigment variety produced

3.10. Antioxidant Activity. It is crucial for eliminating
reactive oxygen species (ROS) to utilize materials with potent
antioxidant or scavenging properties. Regular metabolic
processes generate ROS, leading to various health issues, such
as cancer, diabetes mellitus, and inflammation.52 Reducing
agents can prevent the creation of ROS, rendering them suitable
for treating numerous detrimental illnesses. The effectiveness of
β-CD/Fe3O4NPs in scavenging was evaluated by conducting
experiments on DPPH. The DPPH radical is known for its
stability and is commonly used to assess nanomaterials’
hydrogen (H) donation or radical scavenging capabilities.53
The findings indicated that the DPPH scavenging activity was
elevated proportionally with the rise in the β-CD/Fe3O4NPs
concentration. The highest efficiency in hunting radicals was
observed (347.2 ± 8.2 mg/g) at 100 mg/mL β-CD/Fe3O4NPs,
as illustrated in Figure 9. The superior ability to scavenge
antioxidants may be due to the tiny size of the β-CD/Fe3O4NPs,
as reported in a recent study that the size of the NPs can impact
their scavenging capabilities.54 Furthermore, eliminating free
radicals may be attributed to the transfer of electrons from β-
CD/Fe3O4NPs to free radicals at the nitrogen atom in the center
of the DPPH.55 Furthermore, it may be proposed that the
existence of β-CD, utilized as stabilizers, may additionally
amplify the capability of β-CD/Fe3O4NPs to eliminate
scavengers.56 These were in line with previous research
documenting the enhanced antioxidant activity of inclusion
complexes compared to their raw compounds, such as
myricetin,57 tertiary butylhydroquinone,58 and oligopeptides.59
In summary, the results of this study suggest that the antioxidant
activity of β-CD/ Fe3O4NPs remains intact even after the
formation of inclusion complexes. It appears to be stronger than
that of the unprocessed form.
3.11. Antibacterial Activity. The β-CD/Fe3O4NPs that
were green-produced exhibited superior antibacterial properties
against both Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria in their
natural state. Figure 10a,b displays that E. coli and B. subtilis
growth was inhibited with ZOI 15.0 ± 1.1 and 13.1 ± 2.3 mm,
respectively, compared to positive control that exhibited 12.3 ±
1.5 mm. The effectiveness of β-CD/Fe3O4NPs is greater against
Gram-negative than Gram-positive bacteria. This is conducted
on the cellular composition of both categories. The Gram-
positive external cell wall comprises a dense peptidoglycan layer
that ranges from 20 to 80 nm.60 Polysaccharides can form
chelating complexes with two components found in the thick
peptidoglycan: teichoic and lipoteichoic acids.61 The disintegra-
tion of the bacterial cell membrane is the key factor that leads to
the death of bacterial cells caused by NPs. Consequently, the
discharge of cellular components like amino acids, proteins, and
carbohydrates occurs.62 The results could suggest that β-CD/
Fe3O4NPs are much more active toward examined bacterial
strains. This agrees with the results obtained from earlier studies
which documented that the bacterial strains under examination
showed higher activity when exposed to Fe3O4NPs.63
After analyzing the data above, the antibacterial effect of β-
CD/Fe3O4NPs could potentially impact the biological activity
of bacterial cells. Scheme 1 presents a summary of the potential
antibacterial mechanism of β-CD/Fe3O4NPs based on the

findings as follows: Due to the presence of β-CD/Fe3O4NPs, the
bacterial cell membrane experienced a disturbance, leading to
unstable membrane potential and a breakdown of active
transport. Concurrently, the combination of β-CD/Fe3O4NPs
penetrated the damaged membrane and rendered the enzyme
inactive while disintegrating the DNA, ultimately resulting in the
demise of the bacterial cell wall.64 In addition to the magnetic
properties of β-CD/Fe3O4NPs enabling them to break down the
cellular barrier and infiltrate the bacterial cell, it was
hypothesized that the significant antimicrobial effects might be
attributed to the presence of biomolecules coated on the surface
that originated from β-CD. These biomolecules are believed to
play a crucial role in antimicrobial activity by disrupting the
bacterial cell mechanism.65
4. CONCLUSIONS
The successful synthesis of Fe3O4NPs was achieved by using
supramolecule β-CD as both a reducing and capping agent in
conjunction with the respective metal salt, resulting in the
formation of β-CD/Fe3O4NPs. This can be inferred as a
conclusive finding. Several characterization techniques were
employed to verify the synthesis of β-CD/Fe3O4NPs. The
synthesized β-CD/Fe3O4NPs were utilized for various applica-
tions, including photocatalytic, antioxidant, and antibacterial
activities. The combination of β-CD/Fe3O4NPs demonstrated
exceptional efficacy in the degradation of methylene blue dye.
Furthermore, the combination of β-CD/Fe3O4NPs demon-
strated significant efficacy in antioxidant and antibacterial
